statements.t: In addition, the Company will pay Chevron approximately $200 million in cash and Chevron will contribute to the Company 100% of its consolidated ownership interests in the Company, including 77,827,485 Class B units of the Partnership and 449,000 Class A shares of the Company, all of which will be canceled by the Company.
Although Chevron has committed to minimum volumes under our commercial agreements described above, our results of operations will be impacted by our ability to:
For our terminaling and water gathering systems, the rates will continue to be reset through our annual rate redetermination process through 2033.
For all of our systems, MVCs will continue to provide downside risk protection through 2033.
We expect our ongoing sources of liquidity to include:

Net cash used in investing activities decreased $111.3 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the same period in 2025, primarily driven by completion of our multi-year projects for expansion of compression capacity and the timing of payments for additions to property, plant, and equipment related to ongoing capital projects.
the expected tax treatment of the Transaction and the tax implications of the Transaction for the Company and its shareholders;
our ability to generate sufficient cash flow to pay current and expected levels of distributions;

our ability to comply with government regulations or make capital expenditures required to maintain compliance, including our ability to obtain or maintain permits necessary for capital projects in a timely manner, if at all, or the revocation or modification of existing permits;
our ability to successfully identify, evaluate and timely execute our capital projects, investment opportunities and growth strategies, whether through organic growth or acquisitions;

“We have a solid operational foundation and a sustained track record for generating free cash flow after distributions, which we expect to provide a consistent base for future distributions, capital allocation and shareholder returns.
We expect the transaction announced on October 6, 2026, to close by the end of the year and are excited to transform into a multi-basin, independent midstream company.

The addition of the DJ Basin assets is expected to significantly diversify and increase the footprint of our business, approximately tripling our crude gathering throughput and significantly growing our gas gathering throughput, while also broadening our asset base with ownership in a long-haul crude oil pipeline, all of which positions us well to capture future growth.”
